title: Bandai Releasing 'Tamagotchi Ring' for 30th Anniversary
paragraphs: You had to give it food, play with it and clean up after it — many people who grew up in the 1990s and 2000s will remember having a Tamagotchi.
Now, the digital pet is back — in ring form!
The first Tamagotchi was released by Japanese company Bandai in 1996.
Now, for the Tamagotchi's 30th anniversary, the company has announced a new version that can be worn as a ring.
The ring looks similar to the original Tamagotchi, with an egg-shaped screen and three buttons. But at 28 millimeters long, it's about half the size of the original Tamagotchi.
The ring comes with an adjustable band, so it can fit different finger sizes. Fans can choose to get it in pink and white, blue and gold, or black and silver.
And because it's the 30th anniversary version, users can grow their digital pets into 30 Tamagotchi characters from the past 30 years!
The company said there are also some "secret" characters — but you may only be able to find them if you raise your pet a certain way!
The Tamagotchi ring can be pre-ordered from Bandai's website until October 6. It costs 7,700 yen, or about $48.
The rings will be shipped from February 2027, the company said.
The Tamagotchi ring is the 39th version of the popular digital pet. In 2021, for the Tamagotchi's 25th anniversary, the company released a watch version called the Tamagotchi Smart.
In 2025, Bandai announced that more than 100 million Tamagotchis had been sold around the world.
